::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[max and min of $f(x,y)=\frac{xy+y^2}{x^2+y^2}$](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2499942/max-and-min-of-fx-y-fracxyy2x2y2), asked by [Giulia B.](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/198038/giulia-b) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2017-11-01; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> The function is symmetric because $f(x,y)=f(-x,-y)$. It's defined in $\mathbb{R}^2-\{{(0,0)}\}$.If I calculate the gradient , it's null in the origin. Have I to prove $f$ is limited in $\mathbb{R}^2$?
:::

By the arithmetic mean-geometric mean inequality
$$|xy| \leq \tfrac{1}{2}(x^2 + y^2)$$
so
$$\left|\frac{xy + y^2}{x^2 + y^2}\right| \leq \frac{|xy|}{x^2 + y^2} + \frac{|y|^2}{x^2 + y^2} \leq \frac{1}{2} + 1 = \frac{3}{2}$$
Since $|f(x,y)| \leq \frac{3}{2}$, we know
$$-\frac{3}{2} \leq f(x,y) \leq \frac{3}{2}$$
and $f$ is bounded both above and below.
